Phase A - Internal API Separation (in-tree, no new package):
1. Expand ascii/__init__.py to export all data models and factory functions (w1)
2. Decouple the single `format_scale_factor` import via optional Callable on
   ASCIIChartOptions - the only benchbox import inside ascii/ (w18)
3. Create ascii_api.py facade module as single import point for external callers (w16)
4. Migrate all external callers (CLI, MCP, exporters, post_run_summary,
   chart_generator) to import from ascii_api only (w16)
5. Enforce import boundary with automated gate check (w17)
6. Create golden-output snapshot tests for all 15 chart types BEFORE extraction (w19)
Gate: zero direct ascii submodule imports outside visualization package.

Phase B - Standalone Package Extraction:
7. Scaffold textcharts package in packages/textcharts/ with src layout (w3)
8. Define public API: drop ASCII prefix, add ChartOptions alias (w13)
9. Copy code, rewrite internal imports, add custom palette support (w4-w6)
10. Replace BenchBox ascii/ with compatibility shim re-exporting from textcharts (w7)
11. Add textcharts as BenchBox path dependency (w8)
12. Verify golden-output parity - must be byte-identical (w9-w10)
Gate: full test suite passes, zero benchbox imports in textcharts.

Phase C - Packaging and Release:
13. Complete packaging MVP with README, chart gallery, py.typed (w15)
14. Publish to PyPI and switch BenchBox to versioned dependency (w11)
15. Deprecate compatibility shims after one stable release cycle (w12)
description:
BenchBox currently owns a mature ASCII charting implementation (15 chart types,
595-line base module, zero external dependencies) under
`benchbox/core/visualization/ascii/` plus runtime dispatch and adapters in
CLI/MCP/export paths. We want to extract this into a reusable standalone Python
library called `textcharts` (PyPI: `textcharts`, import: `textcharts`) without
breaking existing BenchBox workflows.

Key architecture decisions:
- Library name: `textcharts` - generic, memorable, no BenchBox branding
- Dispatch layer (`ascii_runtime.py`): stays in BenchBox - it contains
  domain-specific NormalizedResult→chart data conversion
- Naming: standalone drops `ASCII` prefix (e.g. `BarChart` not `ASCIIBarChart`);
  BenchBox shims re-export with `ASCII*` aliases for compatibility
- Only ONE coupling point to sever: `base.py:481` imports `format_scale_factor`

The correct migration path is staged:
1) Define and freeze charting API contracts first
2) Decouple the single `format_scale_factor` import via optional Callable
3) Complete BenchBox-internal API separation before extraction starts
4) Extract charting primitives + renderers behind a compatibility shim
5) Keep BenchBox-specific normalization/adaptation in BenchBox
6) Validate text-output parity via golden snapshot tests before cutover
7) Externalize packaging/release only after in-repo adoption is stable

This TODO captures the full execution DAG required to minimize risk and avoid
regressions in CLI output, MCP responses, and tests.

anti_patterns.dont: change chart IDs or user-facing option names during extraction
anti_patterns.instead: preserve contracts until a separately versioned deprecation plan exists.

anti_patterns.dont: import `benchbox.*` modules inside the standalone package
anti_patterns.instead: use typed adapter DTOs at the BenchBox boundary.

anti_patterns.dont: move BenchBox result normalization models into the standalone library
anti_patterns.why: they encode domain semantics and compatibility obligations

anti_patterns.dont: optimize output formatting during initial extraction
anti_patterns.instead: prioritize strict parity first, then incremental improvements.

anti_patterns.dont: perform a big-bang directory move without shims
anti_patterns.why: this will break imports across CLI/MCP/tests

anti_patterns.dont: start standalone package extraction before internal API-separation gates pass
anti_patterns.why: unresolved internal coupling will leak BenchBox implementation details into the library boundary

work_units.notes:
The single coupling point: `base.py:481` does
`from benchbox.utils.scale_factor import format_scale_factor`.
Strategy:
1. Add `scale_factor_formatter: Callable[[float], str] | None = None` to ASCIIChartOptions
2. In `ASCIIChartBase._render_subtitle` (base.py:479-483): use
   `self.options.scale_factor_formatter(sf)` if set, else fallback to `f"SF={sf}"`
3. Delete the `from benchbox.utils.scale_factor import format_scale_factor` line
4. In `ascii_runtime.py` and `post_run_summary.py`: inject
   `options.scale_factor_formatter = format_scale_factor` before passing to charts
